lessons.title: Recognize AI functions
lessons.subtitle: Function, purpose, data. Not the product name

sections.title: Check functions, not labels
sections.content:
Your spam filter sorts. Your keyboard guesses the next word. Your navigation app prices in the jam. Each can run on machine learning or another AI technique, depending on product and version. Same for image grouping, speech recognition, search ranking.

The product name tells you nothing. A spam filter runs on rules, on statistics, on machine learning, or on all three. Same label, different build.

Write down function, version, configuration. Then purpose, data touched, the unit that answers for it. What you cannot answer technically stays open until the product owner, the documentation or a technical review closes it. Guessing does not count.
sections.keyTakeaway: Function and version count. A product name settles neither the technical nor the legal classification as an AI system.

sections.title: AI functions inside the workday
sections.content:
A case worker has documents read out, the project lead has the meeting transcribed, the buyer translates a supplier mail. Document processing, translation, search, forecasts: AI-supported functions sit anywhere. Whether one is an AI system under the Regulation is decided by how it works and how it is used.

Without an inventory you steer nothing. The list holds function and version, purpose, data, users, owner, approval. Only then can you assign data rules, review duties, training needs.

Article 4 of the EU AI Act, as it stands, obliges providers and deployers to take measures supporting the development of AI literacy in the people who handle the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf. Technical knowledge, experience, education and training, use context and the people or groups affected all count. The Article prescribes no inventory. Without one you do not know the context you are planning for.
sections.keyTakeaway: The inventory carries role- and risk-based AI literacy measures. It does not take the legal and technical assessment of the single case off your hands.

quiz.questionText: A colleague uses suggested replies, a transcription function and a route forecast. What can you record with confidence?

answerOptions.text: None of these functions can contain AI techniques
All three belong in the inventory with version, purpose and data; their classification is still open
Only the transcription can count as an AI-supported function
Record the functions only once their legal classification is finished

quiz.explanation: List first: function, version, purpose, data. Review after. Which entries are AI systems under the Regulation is settled by that review, not by the product name.

quiz.questionText: What does Article 4 of the EU AI Act require of providers and deployers of AI systems?

answerOptions.text: Every company must build its own AI
Every employee must finish a computer science degree
Providers and deployers must take measures supporting the development of AI literacy in people acting on their behalf
Only IT departments may use AI systems

quiz.explanation: No degree, no own AI, no IT monopoly. Article 4 asks for measures supporting the development of AI literacy in people who operate and use AI systems for providers or deployers. Technical knowledge, experience, training, use context and the people affected shape them.

lessons.title: Select AI tools
lessons.subtitle: Edition and configuration, not the brand

sections.title: Compare four operating models
sections.content:
Comparing brands gets you nowhere. Compare the product edition and the operation behind it:

| Operating model | Minimum checks | Typical false conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| **Consumer service** | Terms of use, account settings, retention, training use, legal basis and permitted content | Well known or paid for means approved for company data |
| **Enterprise SaaS** | Contract and DPA, roles and permissions, data region, retention, logging, connectors and training use | The enterprise contract covers every configuration and data class |
| **Local or self-hosted** | Model source, device or infrastructure, patches, telemetry, extensions, access and logging | Local means offline, current and safe |
| **Embedded function** | Concrete function and version, activation, data flows, inherited permissions and owner | Approval of the main product covers every new AI function |

Vendor documentation changes. So do contract terms. Check both at procurement, at every material change, and at the review triggers your organization set.
sections.keyTakeaway: Edition, configuration and approval decide what you may use. An operating model or a brand name assesses nothing.

sections.title: Which tool fits when?
sections.content:
Never ask which tool is best. Ask: for what?

- **Private learning and writing:** A consumer offer can fit if you may share the content and data controls, retention and terms suit the purpose. Placeholders instead of other people. Credentials never belong in a prompt. Never.

- **Work tasks:** Only the product, configuration and workflow approved for this purpose and these data classes. A business subscription is no approval. Neither is an existing company account.

- **Local models:** Local inference can limit data flows. Can. Extensions, telemetry, model downloads, shared machines and weak access controls bring the risk back in.

The whole check, from purpose to approval, comes in Block 2.
sections.keyTakeaway: Free, paid, cloud, local: none is a security class. Purpose, data, rights, contract, configuration and approval decide.

quiz.questionText: You want to draft a private text with an AI assistant. Which statement holds?

answerOptions.text: Only paid business tools are allowed for writing
A consumer offer can fit if you may share the content and data controls, retention and terms suit the purpose
No AI tool may be used to write text
Only the best-known product fits, because a brand determines security

quiz.explanation: Private does not mean it does not matter. Content, rights, data controls, retention and terms decide here too. Placeholders for examples, credentials nowhere.

quiz.questionText: What separates an approved company workflow from any AI subscription?

answerOptions.text: A company workflow always delivers better answers
Approval covers purpose, data classes, contract, configuration, permissions and responsibilities; a subscription does not
A paid subscription may process every data class
Only the provider's EU head office counts

quiz.explanation: An approval is always concrete: this purpose, this edition, this configuration, this data class, these roles. Price, brand and head office check none of it.

lessons.title: Exercise: quick inventory
lessons.subtitle: Ten rows for the functions you really use

sections.title: The AI inventory
sections.content:
Fill in the last columns. A product name alone is not worth a row. Note the function, the provider or deployer, the purpose, the data touched and the responsible unit. Whether a function is legally an AI system is settled by its version and how it works, not by this table.

| No. | Product and function | Purpose | Data touched | Approval known? |
|-----|----------------------|---------|--------------|-----------------|
| 1 | Email: suggested replies | | | |
| 2 | Spreadsheet: assistance or pattern detection | | | |
| 3 | Conferencing software: transcription or assistance | | | |
| 4 | Search engine: AI summary | | | |
| 5 | Email: spam filter | | | |
| 6 | Smartphone keyboard: word prediction | | | |
| 7 | Navigation: route or traffic forecast | | | |
| 8 | | | | |
| 9 | | | | |
| 10 | | | | |

Into the empty rows goes what you really use. Invent nothing. Mark the gaps; product owners, IT or procurement close them.
sections.keyTakeaway: Function, purpose, data, approval, owner: that is what makes an inventory usable. It carries role- and risk-based literacy planning under Article 4.

sections.title: Reading the result
sections.content:
Walk every row again. Function and version, purpose, data, user roles, owner, approval status: miss one and the row is unfinished. Unknowns stay unknown. A guess is not an inventory entry.

Then the open points. Each gets an owner and a next step. The result is a working document. Not a register of every AI system.

Article 4 prescribes no inventory format. A maintained inventory still attaches literacy measures, data rules and review routines to the functions actually in use. Block 2 adds data classes, rights, approvals.
sections.keyTakeaway: Open entries visible, owners named, changes tracked: that keeps an inventory reliable. It steers. Complete evidence under Article 4 it is not.

quiz.questionText: A colleague uses suggested replies, a transcription function and a route forecast. What follows for certain?

answerOptions.text: None of the functions can contain AI
Exactly one AI system, because only transcription uses AI
Exactly three standalone AI systems under the AI Act
The functions belong in the inventory; their technical and legal classification has to be checked against product and version

quiz.explanation: Three functions, three names, zero certainty. AI-supported functions hide inside everyday products, and a name says nothing about how many standalone AI systems sit behind them in law. Record function and version; review afterwards.

quiz.questionText: Why does an AI inventory matter?

answerOptions.text: It is needed for the tax return
Without an inventory you cannot judge which risks exist and which rules apply
It is mandatory only for companies from 250 employees upward
It serves IT budget planning and nothing else

quiz.explanation: Without an inventory you guess. With one you have the base for risk assessment, data rules and responsibilities. It carries governance and literacy measures; on its own it does not meet the EU AI Act's requirements.
